name: Chavín culture
summary: An Andean culture centred on the temple of Chavín de Huántar, high in the Peruvian mountains. Its religious art spread across Peru, uniting many valleys for the first time.

location.value: The Mosna Valley in the northern Andean highlands of Peru, about 3,150 m above sea level.

terrain.value: A mountain valley where two rivers meet, linking the coast and the Amazon lowlands.

climate.value: Cool highland climate with wet and dry seasons.
climate.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

resources.value: Potatoes, quinoa and maize; llamas for transport.
resources.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

disasters.value: Earthquakes and landslides in the Andes.
disasters.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

population.value: No reliable estimate; the temple town may have held a few thousand people.
population.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

urbanisation.value: A town grew around the temple complex at Chavín de Huántar.
urbanisation.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

disease.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

migration.value: Pilgrims travelled to Chavín de Huántar from far away.
migration.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

economicBase.value: Farming improved, with metalwork and textiles developing.

tradeRoutes.value: Exchange between coast, highlands and Amazon (shells, obsidian, cinnabar).
tradeRoutes.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible; the temple held fine goods from far away.
wealth.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

moneyAndTax.value: No money; labour and goods were given to the temple.
moneyAndTax.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

inequality.value: A priestly elite controlled the temple and its rituals.
inequality.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

governmentType.value: A religious centre led by priests rather than a conquest state.
governmentType.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

keyRulers.value: No rulers are known by name; there was no writing.
keyRulers.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

succession.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

institutions.value: An intensified religious cult centred on ceremonial buildings.

stability.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

eliteConflict.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

armyAndTech.value: Little evidence of warfare; influence spread through religion.
armyAndTech.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

majorWars.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

territoryChange.value: Its influence spread to other cultures along the Peruvian coast.

alliancesRivals.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

inventions.value: Improved farming techniques, early metallurgy (gold work) and textiles.

scienceEducation.value: No writing; underground galleries may have used sound and light in rituals.
scienceEducation.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

openness.value: Drew on coastal and Amazonian ideas (jaguars, caimans).
openness.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

religion.value: A cult around a fanged deity, shown in the Lanzón stone.
religion.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

languageWriting.value: No writing; the language is unknown.
languageWriting.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

artsArchitecture.value: The Lanzón stela, the Raimondi Stela and stone heads on the temple walls.
artsArchitecture.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

socialStructure.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

sharedIdentity.value: A shared religious art style across Peru (the “Early Horizon”).
sharedIdentity.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

neighbours.value: Coastal and highland communities in Peru.
neighbours.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

ideasReligions.value: Its religious images (jaguars, snakes, the Lanzón deity) spread across much of Peru.
ideasReligions.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

colonisation.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

riseSignals.value: Developed around 900 BCE at Chavín de Huántar, a meeting point of routes.

peakPeriod.value: About 500 BCE, when the New Temple was built.
peakPeriod.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

declineSignals.value: Unknown; perhaps social change and the rise of regional cultures.
declineSignals.source: Burger, Chavín and the Origins of Andean Civilization (1992)

knownFor.label: Lanzón stela
knownFor.note: A tall carved stone of a fanged god inside the temple.
